### Consolidated Water Advances Permitting for Kalaeloa Seawater Desalination Project in Hawaii


10/21/2026


GEORGE TOWN, Cayman Islands, Oct. 21, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) --[Consolidated Water Co. Ltd.](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=GU1rCa27XdsHcL3d21UTDwoVft0LI1_dJbw_QvEApost7enYp1ARTrf89EhxS5e4oEjdKAlLz0MG70MI3-DG0DJ_T8s7_kh-Ez9apt0AtT4=) (NASDAQ Global Select Market: CWCO), a leading designer, builder, and operator of advanced water treatment plants, today provided an update on permitting and the anticipated construction schedule for its Kalaeloa seawater reverse osmosis desalination project on Oahu, Hawaii.


Since the company’s previous update, the project received approval of its Preservation Plan and Archaeological Monitoring Plan from the State Historic Preservation Division and approval from the Hawaii Department of Health for a Substantial Modification to an Existing Regulated Public Water System. These approvals were required before the company could advance its applications for other permits and approvals.


Several permits and approvals remain outstanding, including a Memorandum of Agreement from the State Historic Preservation Division. Based on the current permitting timeline, Consolidated Water now expects construction to begin in the first half of 2027, compared with its previous expectation of late 2026. The Honolulu Board of Water Supply has granted schedule extensions to reflect the permitting process delays.


In July 2026, the Honolulu Board of Water Supply issued a limited notice to proceed authorizing approximately $6 million for the procurement of long-lead equipment. The early procurement is intended to reduce potential scheduling pressure once the remaining permits and approvals are obtained.


The Kalaeloa facility is being developed under Consolidated Water’s contract to design, build, operate, and maintain a seawater reverse osmosis desalination plant capable of producing 1.7 million gallons of potable water per day. Following commissioning, the company is contracted to operate and maintain the facility for 20 years, with two additional five-year extension options at the client’s discretion.


“We continue to make meaningful progress on the Kalaeloa desalination project,” said Consolidated Water CEO Rick McTaggart. “The recent approvals from the State Historic Preservation Division and the Hawaii Department of Health represent important steps in the permitting process and allow us to advance applications for the remaining permits and approvals. While the permitting timeline has shifted our anticipated construction start to the first half of 2027, the Honolulu Board of Water Supply continues to be supportive and has granted schedule extensions to reflect the process. The limited notice to proceed issued in July is also enabling us to procure long-lead equipment now, which should help the project advance efficiently once the remaining permits and approvals are in place.”


**About Consolidated Water Co. Ltd.**
Consolidated Water Co. Ltd. develops and operates advanced water treatment plants and water distribution systems. The company designs, constructs, and operates seawater desalination facilities in the Cayman Islands, The Bahamas, and the British Virgin Islands, and designs, constructs, and operates water treatment and reuse facilities in the United States.


The company also manufactures and services a wide range of products and provides design, engineering, management, operating, and other services applicable to commercial and municipal water production, supply and treatment, and industrial water and wastewater treatment.
